Going to BTS in December? Singapore Stay Searches Are up 237%
 The DANAMIC Team November 3, 2026 4 minutes read

 If you’re catching BTS in Singapore this December, you’ll share the city with a lot of fans who flew in for it. According to Booking.com , searches for Singapore stays with check-in dates between 16 and 23 December 2026 rose 237% year-on-year , so anyone still weighing a hotel night or a post-show staycation should lock it in soon.
 The searches were made on Booking.com by travellers across APAC (Asia-Pacific) between 22 May and 3 September 2026 , and compared against the same period a year earlier. These are searches rather than confirmed bookings, but they still show where the region’s concert crowd wants to sleep in December.
 The Philippines Leads the Charge
 Booking.com says the Philippines was the top market searching for Singapore stays in that December window, with Australia and India close behind. The fastest growth came from a different mix. Searches from Vietnam, the Philippines, Japan and Thailand jumped more than tenfold year-on-year during the BTS concert period, and Vietnam saw the sharpest rise of all.
 Travellers with luggage walking through an airport terminal “What stood out to us was how quickly travel interest picked up around BTS’ upcoming Singapore concert dates,” said Anthony Lu , Regional Director of Southeast Asia and Greater China at Booking.com, in written responses to DANAMIC. He added that the regional spread “suggests how major concerts can draw fans from across the region to Singapore.”
 For a local fan, the tenfold jump is the number to sit with, because it means a home-town show now carries the pull of a regional event. The ARMY (BTS’s fandom) member beside you in the stands could easily have flown in from Hanoi or Bangkok, and the hotel room down the corridor from yours may well belong to someone from Tokyo.
 Five Acts, One Pattern
 BTS is the headline act, but Booking.com tracked accommodation search demand around the Singapore concert periods of five acts: BTS , BIGBANG , The Weeknd , My Chemical Romance and 5 Seconds of Summer . For each one, the company compared searches during the concert period with the corresponding period a year earlier.
 A packed stadium concert with fans holding up light sticks BIGBANG is the most telling case. Within three weeks of the group announcing its Singapore stop, and before tickets had gone on sale, accommodation searches rose by close to 30% among regional travellers and nearly 32% among international ones. Fans were pricing out rooms before they knew whether they’d land a seat, which is optimism of the most committed kind.
 5 Seconds of Summer pulled interest from much further afield. Searches for Singapore stays rose by close to 130% among travellers from the Netherlands and by over 30% among UK travellers. Put the two side by side and the picture is clear: BTS shows how deep a Singapore date can reach into Asia, while 5SOS shows it can draw fans from as far as Europe too.
 Ticket First, Trip Second
 Two Booking.com-commissioned surveys help explain the behaviour behind those searches. The Travel Happiness Index 2026 polled 10,136 respondents across 10 countries in Asia-Pacific in January 2026, and found that 51% of APAC travellers would add an event, such as a concert, festival, sporting event or exhibition, to a trip to make it feel more worthwhile or better value for money.
 The Travel Trends 2026 report surveyed 32,800 respondents across 34 markets in January 2026, including 800 from Singapore, all leisure travellers who had taken an overnight trip in the past 12 months and planned to travel in 2026. It found that 19% of APAC travellers took a trip for a music concert or festival in 2025, while 27% plan to do so. That eight-point gap between those who went and those planning to go is the figure worth watching, since it points to the concert trip becoming a regular fixture on people’s travel calendars.
 Lu sees the show as only one piece of the plan. “The appeal extends beyond the event itself, with travellers also exploring where to stay, what to eat and what else to experience at the destination,” he said. Put simply, the ticket sets the dates and the rest of the weekend gets built around it.
 What It Means for Locals
 For Singapore fans, the numbers cut both ways. The upside is that your city is the trip everyone else in the region is saving up for, and you get to enjoy that without boarding a plane. The catch is that a hotel night near the show looks far more popular this December than last, judging by that 237% jump in searches between 16 and 23 December.
 If you’ve been toying with a post-concert staycation so you can skip the crush home, the data makes a strong case for booking sooner rather than later. The same logic applies to dinner reservations or any side plans you want to fold into the weekend, because visitors from the Philippines, Australia and India are clearly mapping out the same thing.
 BTS’s December run is when all of this stops being a chart and becomes a crowd, with fans from Vietnam, Japan, Thailand and beyond converging on one city across the same week. If you’re holding a ticket, treat it as the start of a proper mini holiday and search for your 16 to 23 December stay on Booking.com before the rest of the region beats you to it!
